Molecules or ions that can donate protons (H+) in aqueous solution to produce hydronium ions (H₃O+) and pH < 7
terms.to_def: Ko e molekula pe 'ioni 'oku ne lava 'o foaki e polotoni (H+)'i he solusoni vai ke fakatupu ha 'ioni haitoluniumi (H₃O+), pH <7.

terms.en_def: Base like sodium hydroxide (NaOH) dissolves in water to produce alkaline solutions by directly liberating hydroxide ions (OH-) and pH > 7
terms.to_def: Ko e peisi hange ko e NaOH 'oku lava 'o fakamovete he vai mo tukuange hangatonu e 'ioni haitokisaiti (OH-) 'i he vai, pH >7.

terms.en_def: The smallest building block of any element. It is made up of protons & neutrons inside the nucleus with electrons surrounding the nucleus
terms.to_def: Ko e konga si'isi'i taha 'o e elemeniti pea 'oku fa'u'aki e polotoni mo e niutoloni 'i he uho'i 'atomi pea takatakai 'e he 'ilekituloni.

terms.en_def: A characteristic number that determines the identity of an element & the number of protons & electrons in its atom (e.g. ₂₀Ca for Calcium)
terms.to_def: Ko e mata'ifika 'oku ne tala e makehe 'a e elemeniti mo e lahi 'o e polotoni mo e 'ilekituloni he 'atomi takitaha (e.g. ₂₀Ca)

terms.en_def: Molecules or ions than can accept protons (H+) from water to produce hydroxide ions (OH-) and pH > 7
terms.to_def: Ko e molekula pe 'ioni 'oku lava 'o tali e polotoni mei he vai ke ma'u ai e 'ioni haitokisaiti pH >7.

terms.en_def: Solutions or systems whose pH remains relatively constant when small amounts of acid or base are added (e.g. blood buffer)
terms.to_def: Solusoni 'oku ta'eliliu e pH neongo hono tānaki atu e 'esiti pē peisi si'isi'i pe.

terms.en_def: An ion that has a positive charge (e.g. Na+)
terms.to_def: Ko e 'ioni positivi hangē ko e sotiumi Na+.

terms.en_def: The electrode (i.e. inert solid like Platinum, Pt) where reduction occurs in an electrochemical cell.
terms.to_def: Ko e kefote hange ko e palatiumi (Pt) 'oku hoko ai e 'okisikena molia 'i ha sela kemikale'uhila.

terms.en_def: The use of symbols & numbers as subscripts to show the amounts & type of atoms found in a single compound (e.g. rust is Fe₂O₃)
terms.to_def: Ko e ngāue'aki e ngaahi faka'ilonga mo e mata'ifika ke ne tala e lahi 'o e 'atomi 'i ha fo'i komipauni hangē ko e 'ume'umea Fe₂O₃.

terms.en_def: When different chemicals/reactants combine to form new chemicals/products with different compositions (e.g. CH₄ + 2O₂ → CO₂ + 2H₂O)
terms.to_def: Ko e ngaahi liliu fakakemikale kehekehe 'oku nau fanau'i mai e ngaahi komipauni fo'ou hangē ko e CH₄ + 2O₂ → CO₂ + 2H₂O.

terms.en_def: Burning of any substance with oxygen gas which produce carbon dioxide or carbon monoxide, water, heat or light.
terms.to_def: Ko e vela fakakemi mo e 'okisikena ke fakatupu vai, mafana, mo e kaponi tai'okisaiti.

terms.en_def: Substance that contains 2 or more elements that are chemically bonded together in a fixed ratio (e.g. glucose is C₆H₁₂O₆)
terms.to_def: Ko e kemikale fa'u'aki e 'elemeniti 'e 2 pe lahi ange hangē ko e suka lōtaha C₆H₁₂O₆.

terms.en_def: A measure of of the amount of solute in a fixed amount of solvent. Concentration = c = n/V where n =number of moles of solute, V= Volume (L)
terms.to_def: Ko e fua e lahi 'o e soliuti 'i ha soloveni fakatatau ki he 'ekuasi c = n/V ko e n = lahi e soliuti fua he mole, V= Voliume (L).

terms.en_def: A change in the state of matter from gas to liquid (e.g. water vapour in the air changes to liquid water/morning dew)
terms.to_def: Ko e liliu fakakemi 'a e mao ki he vai.

terms.en_def: Any material that allows an electric current or electricity to pass through it (e.g. metals like iron, copper etc.)
terms.to_def: Ko e matelie 'oku ne lava e fakafononga e 'uhila hangē ko e 'aione mo e kopa.

terms.en_def: The flow of electrical energy due to the movement of electrons through a conductor/wire
terms.to_def: Ko e ivi'i 'uhila 'oku fakafononga 'e he 'ilekituloni he uaea 'uhila.

terms.en_def: An aqueous ionic salt solution or molten ionic liquid that conducts electricity (i.e. ions are free to move & conduct electricity)
terms.to_def: Ko e 'ioni vai pē solusoni masima 'oku taka ke fakafononga e ivi'i 'uhila.

terms.en_def: Sub-atomic particles: Each electron has a charge of negative one (-1), a mass close to zero & do not contribute much to the atomic mass
terms.to_def: Ko e tekonga 'atomi 'ilekituloni 'oku nekativi taha (-1) pea ko e ki'i konga si'i pē ia 'o e mamafa e 'atomi.

terms.en_def: A pure substance containing only one type of atom with the same atomic number & mass number (e.g. Carbon, ¹²₆C)
terms.to_def: Ko e 'elemeniti 'oku haohaoa he ko e fa'ahinga 'atomi pē 'e taha 'oku fika 'atomi tatau pe mo hono mamafa hangē koe Kaponi, ¹²₆C.

terms.en_def: A reaction where energy/heat is absorbed from the surrounding (i.e. Energy of the products > Energy of the reactants)
terms.to_def: Ko e liliu fakakemi 'oku ne mimisi mai e ivi mei he 'ātakai.

terms.en_def: A written represenation of a chemical reaction using symbols, chemical formula & numbers to balance (e.g. 2Na + 2H₂O → 2NaOH + H₂ )
terms.to_def: Ko e founga tohi 'o e 'ekuasi fakakemikale 'o ngāue'aki e ngaahi mata'itohi mo e mata'ifika ke fakapalanisi.

terms.en_def: A reversible reaction where the forward & backward reactions occur at the same rate & the concentrations of reactants & products are constant
terms.to_def: Ko e palanisi 'a e liliu fakakemi ki he hoko atu mo e fakafoki mai 'i he taimi tatau pē pea tu'uma'u 'ikai to e liliu 'a hono taufua.

terms.en_def: A change in the state of matter from a liquid into a gas (e.g.steam from boiling water)
terms.to_def: Ko e liliu fakakemi 'a e vai ki he mao.

terms.en_def: A reaction where energy/heat is released to the surrounding (i.e. Energy of the products < Energy of the reactants),
terms.to_def: Ko e liliu fakakemi 'oku ne tukuange mai e ivi ki he 'ātakai.

terms.en_def: Particles are moving rapidly in all directions, high energy & they occupy all the available space.
terms.to_def: Ko e tekonga kasa 'oku 'alu fano ke fakafonu e 'atā kotoa pē.

terms.en_def: Ions are charged particles formed when atoms lose or gain electrons in order to form a stable full outer shell of electrons.
terms.to_def: Ko 'ioni ko e tekonga 'atomi kuo tānaki pe kole mai hono 'ilekituloni ke fakafonu takai 'a tu'a.

terms.en_def: These are different forms of the same element with the same atomic number but different mass number (e.g. ¹²₆C and ¹⁴₆C).
terms.to_def: Ko e fa'ahinga kehekehe 'o e 'elemeniti tatau mo hono fika 'atomi tatau kae kehe 'aupito hono fika mamafa.

terms.en_def: A pH indicator used to determine whether a solution is an acid or base. Acids turn blue litmus paper red. Bases turn red litmus paper blue.
terms.to_def: Pepa 'oku ne fakahaa'i e pH pe ko e 'esiti pē peisi. Ko e 'esiti 'oku ne liliu e pulū ke kulokula. Ko e peisi 'oku ne liliu e kulokula ke pulū.

terms.en_def: Particles move around each other slowly, definite volume, no fixed shape/takes the volume of the container.
terms.to_def: Ko e tekonga vai 'oku fe'unuaki māmālie pē 'i he voliume tatau ka e toki mahino pē hono fōtunga fakatatau ki he fōtunga 'o e me'a 'ai'anga vai.

terms.en_def: There are 3 states of matter: solids, liquid and gas.
terms.to_def: Ko e ngaahi tūkunga 'o e matelie: soliti, vai mo e kasa.

terms.en_def: The temperature where a substance changes phase from a solid to a liquid at normal atmospheric pressure.
terms.to_def: Ko e fua mafana 'oku lava liliu ai e soliti 'o vai.

terms.en_def: Solids with an array of positive metal ions in a "sea" of delocalised electrons (i.e. metallic bond); good conductors, ductible, malleable, high m.p.
terms.to_def: Ko e soliti 'oku laine ai e metali 'ioni positivi mo hono ngaahi hoko fakametali 'o hoko ko e matelie fakafononga 'uhila lelei.

terms.en_def: This is how many moles of solute in one liter of the solution (number of moles = n = m/M where m = mass, M= Molar mass)
terms.to_def: Ko e lahi 'o e tu'oni 'atomi solute he lita 'e taha 'o e solusoni 'o fakatatau ki he 'ekuasi n=m/M.

terms.en_def: A unit of measurement used by chemist to measure the number of particles (atoms, ions etc.). 1 mole = 6.023 x 10²³ particles (i.e. Avogadro's Number)
terms.to_def: Ko e tu'oni 'atomi 'oku fika'i 'aki e lahi 'o e 'atomi pē 'ioni. Mole 'atomi 'e 1 = 'atomi ia 'e 6.023 x 10²³ (Fika Avokato)

terms.en_def: When 2 or more atoms share their electrons & form covalent bonds, they form small new chemical structure (e.g. H₂, NH₃, CO₂)
terms.to_def: Ko e taimi 'oku vahevahe ai 'e he 'atomi 'e 2 pe lahi ange 'a e 'ilekituloni mo e hoko fakakemi ke fa'u'aki ha kemikale fo'ou.

terms.en_def: Use of symbols & numbers in subscript to show the amounts & type of atoms found in a single molecule (e.g. water H₂O)
terms.to_def: Ko e ngāue'aki e ngaahi faka'ilonga mo e mata'ifika 'o e 'atomi 'i ha fo'i molekula 'e taha hangē ko e vai H₂O.

terms.en_def: When the hydronium ion (H₃O+) concentration is the same as the hydroxide (OH-) concentration in aqueous solutions (i.e. pH = 7)
terms.to_def: Ko e taimi 'oku lahi tatau ai e peisi mo e 'esiti 'i ha solusoni pea pH=7.

terms.en_def: Sub-atomic particles: Each neutron has a charge of zero (0), has similar mass to a proton & contributes significantly to the atomic mass
terms.to_def: Ko e tekonga 'atomi niutoloni kotoa pē 'oku noa, pea mamafa tatau mo e polotoni, 'o kaungatonu ki he mamafa faka'atomi.

terms.en_def: This is the center of the atom & contains protons and neutrons. The number of protons & neutrons are used to calculate the atomic mass
terms.to_def: Ko e uho eni 'o e 'atomi 'oku 'i ai e polotoni mo e niutoloni. Ko e lahi 'o e polotoni mo e niutoloni 'oku fika'i 'aki e mamafa faka'atomi.

terms.en_def: It is gain of oxygen, loss of hydrogen, loss of electrons & increase in oxidation number or charge of an ion.
terms.to_def: Oku tānaki mai e 'okisikena, kae mole atu e 'ilekituloni pea fakalahi e fika 'okisaiti pe 'ioni.

terms.en_def: An ordered arrangement of ~118 elements into groups & periods according to their atomic numbers, electronic configuration & properties
terms.to_def: Ko e tēpile 'oku tu'u fakahokohoko ai e ngaahi 'elemeniti 'e 118 'o fakakulupu fakatatau ki he fika faka'atomi mo e naunau 'ilekituloni.

terms.en_def: A measure of the [H₃O+ ] concentration in aqueous solutions: pH = -log₁₀[H₃O+ ]. The pH scale is from 1to 14. Acids:pH<7, Base: pH>7
terms.to_def: Ko e me'afua 'esiti mo e peisi. pH mei he 1-14. Ko e 'esiti 'oku pH < 7 pea peisi 'oku pH > 7 pea lava ke fika'e pH = -log₁₀[H₃O+ ].

terms.en_def: An insoluble solid (s) formed when two different solutions are mixed (e.g. PbI₂ (s) is formed from mixing lead nitrate & KI solutions).
terms.to_def: Ko e soliti mei he fefiohi fakakemi 'a e solusoni 'e 2.

terms.en_def: Each proton has a charge of positive one (+1), has similar mass to a neutron & contributes significantly to the atomic mass
terms.to_def: Ko e tekonga 'atomi polotoni 'oku positivi 'e taha (+1) pea mamafa tatau mo e niutoloni 'e taha pea kaungatonu ki he mamafa 'o e 'atomi.

terms.en_def: It is the loss of oxygen, gain of Hydrogen, gain of electrons & decrease in oxidation number or charge of an ion.
terms.to_def: Ko e mole atu 'a e 'okisikena, kae tānaki mai 'a e haitokena, 'ilekituloni, mo e holo 'a e fika 'okisaiti pē 'ioni.

terms.en_def: Particles vibrate around a fixed position, fixed shape, fixed volume & rigid/cannot be compressed easily.
terms.to_def: Ko e tekonga soliti 'oku ngaungaue he potu, fōtunga mo e voliume tu'uma'u pea 'ikai ke malomi ngofua.

terms.en_def: This is the solid component of a solution (e.g. aqueous sugar solution, sugar is the solute)
terms.to_def: Ko e konga soliti 'o ha solusoni.

terms.en_def: A solution is formed by dissolving a solute in a solvent (e.g. salt solution is formed by dissolving salt/solute in the water/solvent).
terms.to_def: Ko e solusoni 'oku fa'u 'e he solute tānaki ki he soloveni.

terms.en_def: This is the liquid component of a solution (e.g. aqueous sugar solution, water is the solvent)
terms.to_def: Ko e tekonga vai 'o ha solusoni.

terms.en_def: Any small piece of matter like protons, neutrons and electrons that make up atoms.
terms.to_def: Ko e kongokonga 'atomi hangē ko e polotoni, niutoloni mo e 'ilekituloni.

terms.en_def: A change in the state of matter from solid to gas without changing to a liquid first (e.g. Iodine)
terms.to_def: Ko e liliu fakakemi 'a e soliti ki he kasa.

terms.en_def: A analytical technique in the lab that uses a standard solution (usually a base) to determine the unknown concentration of an acid
terms.to_def: Ko e founga fakakemi 'o e fehu'i'aki 'o e peisi mo e 'esiti ke 'ilo e taufua 'o e 'esiti.

terms.en_def: The rate at which an object changes its velocity (i.e. speeds up, slows down or changes direction). Equation: a = Δv/Δt
terms.to_def: Ko e vave 'o e liliu 'o e 'alu hake pe ko e hifo tuai pe fetongi hala fononga 'o hangē ko e 'ekuasi a = Δv/Δt.

terms.en_def: A type of radiation sent out by radioactive elements which consist of alpha (α) particles that are high speed nuclei of helium (⁴₂He²+)
terms.to_def: Ko e fa'ahinga huelo 'oku tuku atu 'e he 'elemeniti mo'ui 'oku 'i ai e tekonga 'alifa 'oku vave fau hono uho'i 'atomi heliumi (⁴₂He²+).

terms.en_def: This is "how high" a wave is or the maximum displacement of a wave from its rest /equilibrium position
terms.to_def: Ko e ma'olunga 'o e peau mei he laine mālōlō.

terms.en_def: The pressure exerted by the weight of air in the atmosphere of the earth (Pressure = Force/Area, i.e Pressure is Force per unit Area)
terms.to_def: Ko e ta'au 'o e 'ea mei he 'atimosifia 'o e mamani 'o hangē ko e 'ekuasi P = Force/Area

terms.en_def: A force that is exerted between two objects that are in physical contact or touching each other (e.g. Applied force; pushing a box)
terms.to_def: Ko e ivi ta'omi mei he ongo me'a 'e 2 'oku na fefa'uhi fakasino.

terms.en_def: This refers to the flow of electric charge from the positive terminal (+) of a power source/battery to the negative terminal (-).
terms.to_def: Ko e fetafeaki 'a e ivi 'uhila mei he pou positivi ki he pou nekativi 'o e maka kasa.

terms.en_def: This is when the speed of an object slows down & the acceleration becomes negative (e.g. a = - 15 m/s²)
terms.to_def: Ko e holo e vave 'o e lele 'a ha me'a pea nekativi leva e liu vave.

terms.en_def: This is mass per unit volume of a substance (Density = Mass/Volume) or the ratio of the mass of a substance to its volume.
terms.to_def: Ko e fua mā'opo'opo 'o fakatatau ki he 'ekuasi ko e D=M/V pē ko e falakiseni 'o e mamafa ki hono voliume.

terms.en_def: The current or electric charge that moves constantly in a one direction only (e.g. battery). Also known as DC current.
terms.to_def: Ko e tafe 'a e ivi 'uhila tu'uma'u ki he feitu'u pē 'e taha hangē ko e maka kasa.

terms.en_def: This is a device used to convert chemical energy into electrical energy (also known as an electrochemical cell).
terms.to_def: Ko e me'angāue 'oku ne liliu e ivi kemikale ki he ivi'i 'uhila.

terms.en_def: The rate at which charge flows pass a point in an electric circuit. Electric Current = I = Q/t where Q = quantity of charge, t = time
terms.to_def: Ko e vave 'o e tafe 'ae ivi 'uhila 'i he fatakamilo 'uhila 'o hangē ko e 'ekuasi I=Q/t.

terms.en_def: The piece of metal used to connect the solution & the circuit in an electrochemical cell. E.g. Anodes (-) & Cathodes (+).
terms.to_def: Ko e metali 'oku ne fakahoko 'a e solusoni ki he fakatakamilo 'uhila hangē ko e Anote (-) mo e Kefote (+).

terms.en_def: Waves cause by oscillations of electric & magnetic field & are able to travel through a vacuum (e.g. light).
terms.to_def: Kaupeau fakatupu 'e he femalele'aki 'a e ivi 'uhila mo e makineti pea 'oku lava 'o fakafononga he 'āngoa.

terms.en_def: The non-contact electric force between charged particles. It can be attractive (e.g. + & - charges) or repulsive (+ & + or - & - charges).
terms.to_def: Ko e ivi 'uhila mei he naunau tekonga 'oku fetokanga'aki (positivi pe nekativi) pe fesītu'a'aki (positivi pe nekativi).

terms.en_def: Any push or pull exerted on an object measured in Newtons (N)
terms.to_def: Ko e ivi fusi pe teke 'oku ta'omi ki ha me'a. 'Okou fua'aki e 'iuniti Niutoni (N).

terms.en_def: The number of waves passing any point each second. Frequency (measured in Hz) = f = T/1 where T = Period (measured in seconds).
terms.to_def: Ko e lahi 'o e peau kuo fakalaka 'i ha poini he sekoni 'e taha 'o hangē ko e 'ekuasi F= T/1.

terms.en_def: When two surfaces are in contact, there is a force that resists movement. This force is known as Friction.
terms.to_def: I he taimi 'oku fetaulaki ai ha ongo tafa'aki 'e 2 pea 'oku 'i ai e malohi faka'apulu e ngāue.

terms.en_def: A fuse contains a thin wire which melts if the electric current is too high (i.e. a small electrical safety device)
terms.to_def: Ko e fiusi ko e ki'i uaea manifi 'oku vaia kapau 'oku fu'u mālohi e 'uhila tafe.

terms.en_def: Reaction where two smaller nuclides combine into one larger nuclide & release energy
terms.to_def: Ko e fakataha'i 'a e nukilaiti iiki 'e 2 ke ma'u ai e taha lahi mo e ivi.

terms.en_def: High energy electromagnetic radiation so has no mass & no charge (i.e. is part of the electromagnetic spectrum)
terms.to_def: Ko e ivi ma'olunga 'uhilamakineti 'oku 'ikai hano mamafa, positivi pe nekativi.

terms.en_def: This is another way of expressing the slope (i.e. how steep a straight line is). Gradient = rise/run
terms.to_def: Ko e founga 'e taha hono fakamatala'i e tahakehake hangē ko e 'ekuasi G=rise/run.

terms.en_def: The force of gravity (Fg) that exists between earth & the objects that are near it, causing objects to accelerate (i.e. g = 9.81 m/s²)
terms.to_def: Ko e māloohi 'o e kalāvite he vaha'a 'o mamani mo e me'a ofi ki ai 'o fakatupu 'enau liu vave pea ta'eliliu mei he 9.81 m/s².

terms.en_def: Time taken for half the radioactive atoms in a sample to decay
terms.to_def: Ko e taimi 'oku 'aunga ai e vaeua 'o e huelo faka'atomi.

terms.en_def: The change in momentum (Δp) produced by a force (F) acting for a length of time (t). Impulse = I = Δp = FΔt
terms.to_def: Ko e liliu e takina fakatupu 'e he malohi 'oku ngāue ki he fa'ahinga taimi 'o hangē ko e 'ekuasi I = Δp = FΔt.

terms.en_def: Materials that do not allow the free flow of electrons or electrical current (e.g. plastic). Insulator is the opposite of a conductor.
terms.to_def: Ko e matelia 'oku tapu ke ne fakafononga e 'ilekituloni pe 'uhila tafe hangē ko e pelesitiki.

terms.en_def: Energy possessed by an object due to its motion. Kinetic Energy = Ek = ½ mv² where m = mass, v = velocity
terms.to_def: Ko e ivi ngāue 'o ha me'a hangē ko e 'ekuasi Ek = ½ mv².

terms.en_def: The region around a magnet in which a magnetic force is exerted (i.e. where iron or other magnets experience a force)
terms.to_def: Ko e 'elia fakamakineti mei he malohi 'o ha makineti.

terms.en_def: The quantity of matter in an object. The unit of mass is kg or g (1kg is the mass of 1 liter of water at about 4°C).
terms.to_def: Ko e kakano 'o e matelie: ko e 1kg 'oku tatau ia 'o e lita vai 'e 1 he 4°C.

terms.en_def: The study of motion of objects & equilibrium. Kinematics (motion) & Dynamics (forces) are the two main branches of Mechanics.
terms.to_def: Ko e saienisi 'o e me'a 'oku ngaue, nga'unu pea palanisi. 'Oku konga lalahi e 2 ko e Kinamatika mo e Tainamika

terms.en_def: The product of the mass and velocity of a moving object or body. Momentum = p = mv
terms.to_def: Ko e takina 'oku fika'i mei he kakano mo e vave 'o e ngaue 'a ha me'a 'o hangē ko e 'ekuasi p = mv.

terms.en_def: The Standard International (SI) unit of force. A force of one newton (1 N) will give an object of mass 1 kg an acceleration of 1 m/s².
terms.to_def: Ko e 'iuniti Niutoni 'a e malohi 'o e teke pe fusi. Ko e niutoni 'e 1 te ne 'ave 'a e mamafa 1kg 'aki e vave ko e 1 m/s².

terms.en_def: The energy released when the nuclei of large atoms split apart (i.e. fission reaction) or when smaller nuclei combine in fusion reactions.
terms.to_def: Ko e ivi faka'atami ne pu'aki mai 'e he uho'i 'atomi lalahi ne mavaeua.

terms.en_def: The relationship between voltage (V), resistance (R) and current (I) is given by Ohm's Law: V=IR
terms.to_def: Ko e lao 'a 'Oumi ko e vā 'o e volota, taliteke'i mo e 'uhila tafe.

terms.en_def: The regular, repeating path that one object in space takes around another one due to the force of gravity (e.g.planets orbit the sun)
terms.to_def: Ko e vilovilo tu'uma'u 'a e me'a 'i he 'atā 'o fakatatau ki he malohi 'o e kalāvite.

terms.en_def: Power = P = W/t where W=Work, t=time. Power is the rate at which work is done.
terms.to_def: Ko e ivi malohinga 'o ha me'a ko e vave 'oku lava 'osi ki ai e ngāue 'o hangē ko e 'ekuasi P=W/t

terms.en_def: Pressure = P = F/A or force per area in N/m².
terms.to_def: Ko e malohi 'oku ne ta'omi ha 'elia 'o hange ko e 'ekuasi P=F/A

terms.en_def: Isotopes with unstable nuclei/parent nuclei which can spontaneously emit particles or radiation leaving new nuclei/daughter nuclei
terms.to_def: Ko e 'isotope uho'i 'atomi ta'emanofo 'oku ne lava 'o pu'aki mai e tekonga 'atomi pe ivi'i 'atomi.

terms.en_def: Reaction force exists at the same time as the Action force with equal magnitudes but they act in opposite directions (i.e. Newton's 3rd Law).
terms.to_def: Ko e ivi fakafoki 'o e ivi ngāue he taimi tatau, 'aki 'a e malohi tatau ka ko e feitu'u fehangahangai (Ko e Lao hono 3 ia 'a Niutoni)

terms.en_def: The change in speed & direction when light or waves travels from one mediem to another (e.g. from air to water)
terms.to_def: Ko e liliu 'o e vave mo e feitu'u he taimi 'oku fononga ai e maama pe peau mei he matelie 'e taha ki he taha.

terms.en_def: It's how much an electrical component restricts the flow of current. The lower the resistance (R) the better the current flows.
terms.to_def: Ko e taliteke'i 'o e 'uhila tafe.

terms.en_def: The amount of heat required to raise the temperature of 1 kg of the substance by 1 degree Celsius (e.g. water, c = 4180 J kg‾¹ °C‾¹)
terms.to_def: Ko e māfana 'oku fiema'u ke fakamāfana'i e matelie 1kg 'aki e tikilī 'e taha.

terms.en_def: It's how fast an object is travelling & it's a scalar quantity (i.e. direction is not important). Speed = v = d/t where d = distance, t = time
terms.to_def: Ko e vave 'o e fakafononga 'o ha me'a hangē ko e 'ekuasi v=d/t. Ko e fononga ki ha fa'ahinga feituu pe (e.g. 5 m/s)

terms.en_def: The pulling force in a rope/string when stretched under an external force (e.g. ball hanging on a string, tension force equals the weight force)
terms.to_def: Ko e ivi falō 'o ha maea he taimi 'oku falō ai 'e ha ivi fakatu'a.

terms.en_def: Derived from the Greek word "therme" which means heat. Heat is used to denote thermal energy (which is really kinetic energy).
terms.to_def: Ko e ivi māfana ko e ma'u mei he lea Kalisi.

terms.en_def: Waves where the particles of the medium oscillate or vibrate at right angles or 90° to the direction the waves are travelling.
terms.to_def: Ko e peau 'oku vilovilo hono tekonga 'atomi tikilī 'e 90 ki he feitu'u 'oku fononga ki ai e peau.

terms.en_def: Uncertainty of a single measurement is given by the least count of the measuring instrument (e.g. 10.5 ± 0.1 mm if vernier calliper is used).
terms.to_def: Oku veiveiua 'a e fua tu'otaha 'o ha me'a. 'Oku fakafuofua'i ia mei he fua si'isi'i taha 'o e me'angaue.

terms.en_def: Refers to a space devoid of matter & is characterized by the absence of air & other gases (i.e. no particles, pressure = 0)
terms.to_def: Ko e feitu'u 'oku hala'atā ha matelie 'i ai na'a mo e 'ea.

terms.en_def: The speed in a given direction & it's a vector quantity measured in m/s. Velocity = v = d/t where d = displacement, t=time
terms.to_def: Ko e vave 'o e fononga ki ha feitu'u pea mo hono taimi hangē ko e 'ekuasi v= d/t (e.g. 5 m/s North)

terms.en_def: The distance between two successive corresponding positions in a wave (e.g. distance between two successive crests or troughs)
terms.to_def: Ko e vaha'a kaupeau 'e 2 hokohoko 'oku fua mei he poini tatau.

terms.en_def: The force (F) applied times the distance moved by the object in the direction of the force. Work = W = F×d where d=displacement
terms.to_def: Ko e ngāue 'oku fika'i ia mei he lahi e malohi 'oku faka'aonga'i ke ue'i ha me'a ki he feitu'u tatau 'o hangē ko e 'ekuasi W=Fxd.

terms.tongan: Fakalelei fai 'e Sisu he vaa 'o e 'Otua mo e tangata
terms.en_def: The reconciliation between God and humans brought about by the sacrificial death of Jesus Christ
terms.to_def: Ko e fakalelei 'i he vā 'o e 'Otua mo e tangata makatu'ung ahe feilaulau na'e fai 'e Kalaisi Sisu he'ene pēkia.

terms.en_def: God’s act of removing the guilt and penalty of sin while at the same time declaring a sinner righteous through Christ’s atoning sacrifice.
terms.to_def: Ko hono to'o 'e he 'Otua 'a e mo'ua mo e tautea 'o e angahala pea lau ai e taha angahala kuo angatonu tu'unga he fakalelei kuo fai 'e Kalaisi.

terms.en_def: The process of being made holy, leading to a life of holiness and separation from sin.
terms.to_def: Ko e ngaohi ke mā'oni'oni pea a'u ki he mo'ui mā'oni'oni 'o mahu'i mei he angahala.

terms.en_def: The Christian doctrine that defines God as three consubstantial persons, the Father, the Son (Jesus Christ), and the Holy Spirit.
terms.to_def: Ko e tokāteline fakakalisitiane ko e 'Otua mo hono fakahā'anga 'e 3 ko e Tamai, 'Alo, mo e Laumālie Mā'oni'oni.

terms.en_def: The Christian belief that God became flesh, embodied in Jesus Christ, as both fully divine and fully human.
terms.to_def: Ko e hoko 'o kakano 'a e 'Otua 'ia Sisu Kalaisi, 'o 'Otua mo tangata fakatou'osi.

terms.en_def: The Christian belief that Jesus rose from the dead on the third day after his crucifixion, signifying victory over sin and death.
terms.to_def: Ko e Tui Fakakalisitiane na'e toetu'u 'a Sisu mei he pēkia hili 'a e 'aho 'e 3 hono kalusefai, ko e fakamo'oni kuo Ne ikuna'i e angahala mo e mate.

terms.en_def: The action of saving or being saved from sin, error, or evil through Jesus’ sacrifice.
terms.to_def: Ko e ngāue fakahaofi mei he angahala, kovi mo e tēvolo makatu'unga he feilaulau na'e fai 'e Sisu.

terms.en_def: Deliverance from sin and its consequences, believed by Christians to be brought about by faith in Christ.
terms.to_def: Ko e fakahaofi mei he angahala mo hono nunu'a, koe'uhi ko e tui kia Kalaisi 'o fakatatau ki he tui 'a e kau kalisitiane.

terms.en_def: The free and unmerited favor of God, as manifested in the salvation of sinners and the bestowal of blessings.
terms.to_def: Ko e 'alo'ofa tu'unga'a pē 'a e 'Otua 'o fou mai 'i hono fakamolemole'i e kau angahala mo fai honau tāpuekina.

terms.en_def: Complete trust or confidence in God and the doctrines of the Christian religion, especially the saving faith in Christ.
terms.to_def: Ko e tui pikitai ki he 'Otua, 'o hangē ko e Tui Fakakalisitiane, ko e hao ia mei he 'auha he ko e tui kia Kalaisi.

terms.en_def: The action of repenting; sincere regret or remorse for wrongdoing or sin.
terms.to_def: Ko e fakatomala mo e ongo'i mamahi mo'oni he faikovi pē angahala.

terms.en_def: The doctrine stating that sin entered the human world through Adam and Eve’s disobedience to God, and all human beings inherit a sinful nature.
terms.to_def: Ko e tokāteline 'o e hū 'a e angahala ki he fa'ahinga 'o e tangta he talangata'a 'a 'Ivi mo 'Atama he kamata'anga.

terms.en_def: The doctrine that all events have been willed by God, usually with reference to the eventual fate of the individual soul.
terms.to_def: Ko e tokāteline ko e hoko mai 'a e me'a kotoa kuo 'osi tokateu pē 'e he 'Otua.

terms.en_def: The part of theology concerned with death, judgment, and the final destiny of the soul and of humankind.
terms.to_def: Ko e teolosia fekau'aki mo e mate, fakamaau mo e iku'anga 'o e laumālie 'o e fa'ahinga 'o e tangata.

terms.en_def: Often synonymous with the end times, referring to the revelation of God’s will and the unfolding of divine judgment and salvation.
terms.to_def: I he kuonga faka'osi, 'oku fakahā ai 'e he 'Otua hono finangalo 'ene fai fakamaau mo 'ene fai fakamo'ui.

terms.tongan: Ko e Toe ha'ele mai 'a Sisu Kalaisi
terms.en_def: The anticipated return of Jesus to earth, prophesied in the New Testament, to fulfill the rest of Messianic prophecy.
terms.to_def: Ko e 'amanaki ki he toe hā'ele mai 'a Sisu ki mamani ke fakakakato 'a e palofisaiki he Mīsaia, hangē ko ia na'e kikite'i he Fuakava Fo'ou.

terms.en_def: A theological concept where believers are said to be taken up to heaven either prior to or during the tribulation.
terms.to_def: Ko e teolosia hono 'ave e kakai tui ki Hevani kimu'a pē lolotonga e Fakamamahi Lahi.

terms.en_def: A future period of time when suffering and persecution will reach a peak before the end of the world and the Second Coming of Christ.
terms.to_def: Ko e taimi 'o e mamahi lahi kimu'a he 'osi 'a māmani, mo e toe hā'ele mai 'a Sisu.

terms.en_def: The 1000-year reign of Christ on earth, a concept based on Revelation 20, with differing views on its timing relative to Christ’s return.
terms.to_def: Ko e ta'u 'e 1000 'e pule ai 'a Kalaisi 'i māmani 'i ha'ane toe foki mai Fakahā vahe 20.

terms.en_def: A figure who will emerge in the end times, opposing Christ and deceiving many.
terms.to_def: Ko e tokotaha te ne fakafepaki'i 'a Kalaisi he kuonga faka'osi, pea mo kākā'i e tokolahi.

terms.en_def: Symbolic figures in the book of Revelation, often associated with the Antichrist and systems of political and religious oppression.
terms.to_def: Ko e taha 'oku hangē ha manufekai 'oku poupou ki he taha te ne fakafepaki kia Kalaisi he me'a fakapule'anga mo fakalotu.

terms.en_def: A figure associated with the Antichrist who will perform signs and lead people away from the truth.
terms.to_def: Ko e palōfita loi, 'e poupou kia Malakilaopē ko Fakafepaki kia Kalaisi pea mo mo'oni.

terms.en_def: The site of a final battle between the forces of good and evil, predicted in the book of Revelation.
terms.to_def: Ko e mala'etau 'e fepaki faka'osi ai e lelei mo e kovi 'oku talanoa ki ai e Tohi Fakahā.

terms.en_def: The time when God will judge the living and the dead, rewarding the faithful and punishing the wicked.
terms.to_def: Ko e taimi 'e fakamāu'i ai 'e he 'Otua 'a e mo'ui mo e mate, 'o fakapale'i 'a e kau failelei, kae tautea 'a e kau faikovi.

terms.en_def: The Christian belief that the dead will be raised and reunited with their souls at the end of time.
terms.to_def: Ko e Tui Fakakalisitiane 'e toetu'u e mate' 'i he 'aho fakamui.

terms.en_def: The eternal dwelling place of God and the final abode for the righteous.
terms.to_def: Ko e feitu'u 'oku 'afio ai 'a e 'Otua pea 'e nofo foki ai 'a e kau mā'oni'oni.

terms.tongan: Heli, Potu 'o e tangi & fengai'itaki 'o e nifo
terms.en_def: The place of eternal punishment for the wicked
terms.to_def: Ko e feitu'u 'e tautea ta'engata ai 'a e kau faikovi.

terms.en_def: The heavenly city, described in Revelation, where God will dwell with His people in the new heaven and new earth.
terms.to_def: Ko e kolo fakahevani fo'ou 'e 'afio ai 'a e 'Otua he'ene hā'ele mai ki mamani.

terms.tongan: Hevani fo'ou mo e mamani fo'ou
terms.en_def: The renewed creation where God will reside with His people, free from sin and suffering, as described in Revelation 21.
terms.to_def: Ko e Hevani Fo'ou mo e Mamani Fo'ou kuo fakatupu 'e he 'Otua ke 'afio ai mo hono kakai 'o 'ikai ha angahala pe ha faingata'a fakatatau ki he Tohi Fakahā vahe 21.

terms.en_def: Refers to the final trumpet blast signaling the end of the world and the resurrection of the dead.
terms.to_def: Ko e talupite 'e ifi he ngata'anga 'o mamani pea 'e toetu'u hake 'a e mate.

terms.en_def: Described in Revelation as the final place of punishment for the devil, his followers, and the wicked.
terms.to_def: Ko e anoafi 'e tautea ai e tēvolo, hono kau muimui mo e kau faikovi.

terms.en_def: A heavenly record of those who are saved and granted eternal life with God.
terms.to_def: Ko e Tohi 'oku hiki ai kinautolu kuo fakahaofi pea nau a'usia 'a e mo'ui ta'engata 'i he 'ao 'o e 'Otua.

terms.tongan: Taloni lahi hinehina 'o e Tu'I Fakamaau
terms.en_def: The final judgment of all souls by Christ, as described in Revelation.
terms.to_def: Ko e Fakamaau Tuku 'e fai 'e Kalaisi 'oku talanoa ki ai e Tohi Fakahā.

terms.en_def: An early statement of Christian belief that summarizes core Christian doctrines, including the Trinity and the resurrection.
terms.to_def: Ko e Tui Fakakalisitiane fekau'aki mo e tokāteline 'o e Tolu Taha'i 'Otua mo e toetu'u 'o e mate.

terms.en_def: A Protestant principle that the Bible alone is the ultimate authority in matters of faith and practice.
terms.to_def: Ko e Tui Fakapalotisani ko e Tohitapu' pē 'a e fakahinohino pau fekau'aki mo e tui mo e ngāue 'a e kalisitiane.

terms.en_def: The Protestant doctrine that faith alone, apart from works, justifies the sinner before God.
terms.to_def: Ko e Tui Fakapalotisani ko e tui', pē 'o 'ikai makatu'unga ha ngāue, 'oku fakatonuhia ai ha angahala 'e he 'Otua.

terms.en_def: The belief that salvation comes by divine grace or unmerited favor only, not as something merited by the sinner.
terms.to_def: Ko e tui ko e fakamo'ui' ko e kelesi pē 'a e 'Otua 'o 'ikai makatu'unga ha ngāue 'a ha taha angahala.

terms.en_def: The set form of public worship, particularly in Christian church services.
terms.to_def: Ko e fakahokohoko'o e ngaahi ouau lotu fai 'i ha Siasi Fakakalisitiane.

terms.en_def: Also known as Communion or the Lord’s Supper; a sacrament commemorating the Last Supper of Jesus Christ with his disciples.
terms.to_def: Ko e ouau 'o e Sākalameniti 'o e 'Ohomohe, ko e fakamanatu e 'ohomohe faka'osi 'a Sisu mo 'ene kau ako'.

terms.en_def: A sacrament of initiation into the Christian faith, involving water as a symbol of purification.
terms.to_def: Ko e faka'ilonga 'o e fanau'ifo'ou 'i he Tui Fakakalisitiane 'o faka'ilonga'i e fakama'a mei he angahala 'aki e Papitaiso Vai.

terms.en_def: A short hymn of praises to God in various forms of Christian worship.
terms.to_def: Ko e himi fakafeta'i nounou he kamata'anga 'o ha malanga pē feohi'anga lotu fakakalisitiane.

terms.en_def: A blessing pronounced by the minister at the end of a service.
terms.to_def: Ko e tāpuaki faka'osi 'i ha ouau feohi'anga fakalotu fakakalisitiane.

terms.en_def: The table in a Christian church at which the bread and wine are consecrated in the Eucharist.
terms.to_def: Ko e tēpile 'i ha Siasi Fakakalisitiane 'oku fakatāpui ai e mā mo e uaine 'o e Sākalameniti 'o e 'Ohomohe.

terms.tongan: Fakahokohoko e ng. Folofola ke lau he lotu
terms.en_def: A book or listing that contains a collection of scripture readings appointed for Christian worship on a given day or occasion.
terms.to_def: Ko e Tohi Lotu 'oku lau mei ai e folofola ki ha feohi'anga lotu fakakalisitiane.

terms.en_def: The central act of worship in the Roman Catholic Church, which includes the celebration of the Eucharist.
terms.to_def: Ko e misa he lotu 'a e Siasi Katolika, 'a ia 'oku fai ai e Sākalameniti 'o e 'Ohomohe.

terms.en_def: A journey to a sacred place as an act of religious devotion, seeking closeness with God or to venerate a holy site.
terms.to_def: Ko e fononga ki ha feitu'u toputapu ke fai ai ha lotu mo ha feohi mo e 'Otua.

terms.tongan: Hemiti, nofo tokotaha ke fai 'ene lotu
terms.en_def: A person who lives in seclusion from society, usually for religious reasons, to pursue an ideal of total dedication to God.
terms.to_def: Ko e taha 'oku nofo tokotaha 'i ha feitu'u ke lotu mo feohi mo e 'Otua.

terms.en_def: A person who believes that nothing is known or can be known of the existence or nature of God.
terms.to_def: Ko e taha 'oku ta'elotu, ko 'ene tui' 'oku 'ikai lava ha taha 'o 'ilo 'a e 'Otua.

terms.en_def: The process of learning to follow Jesus Christ more closely, often involving mentorship and practicing spiritual disciplines.
terms.to_def: Ko e ako ke lava 'o muimui ofi kia Sisu, mo tokanga makehe ke tupu 'ene mo'ui fakakalisitiane.

terms.en_def: The anticipated savior of the Jews, prophesied in the Old Testament, whom Christians identify as Jesus Christ.
terms.to_def: Ko e tokotaha 'oku 'amanaki ki ai e kau Siu' 'e ha'u ko e Mīsaia 'o hangē kuo 'osi kikite'i he Fuakava Motu'a, ka ko Sisu Kalaisi he lau 'a e kau kalisitiane.

terms.en_def: Abdomen: The part of the body containing the digestive organs, bounded by the diaphragm and the pelvis.
Abdomen Lower: The lower portion of the abdomen, below the navel.
Abdomen Lower Part Of: Refers to the specific region in the lower area of the abdomen.
Abdomen Upper Part Of: The upper portion of the abdomen, above the navel.
Achilles Tendon: The tendon connecting the calf muscles to the heel bone.
Adam's Apple (laryngeal prominence): The protrusion in the neck, formed by the thyroid cartilage of the larynx.
Adrenal gland: A small organ on top of each kidney that produces hormones like adrenaline and cortisol.
Albumin: A protein found in blood plasma, essential for maintaining the osmotic pressure needed for proper distribution of body fluids.
Alveoli (air sacs in the lungs): Tiny sacs within our lungs that allow oxygen and carbon dioxide to move between the lungs and bloodstream.
Ankle: The joint connecting the foot with the leg.
Ankle/Ankle Bone: Refers to the bones forming the ankle joint, primarily the talus bone.
Anus: The opening at the end of the digestive tract through which solid waste leaves the body.
Aorta: The largest artery in the body, originating from the left ventricle of the heart and extending down to the abdomen.
Appendix: A small tube-like structure attached to the large intestine, with no known essential function.
Arch: Refers to the curved part of the foot, also known as the arch of the foot.
Areola: The pigmented area surrounding the nipple of the breast.
Arm: The upper limb of the body, extending from the shoulder to the wrist.
Armpit: The area under the joint where the arm connects to the shoulder, also known as the axilla.

terms.tongan: kālava, kālava kini - 'ave toto mei he mafu ki he sino kotoa
terms.en_def: Arteries: Blood vessels that carry oxygenated blood away from the heart to the rest of the body.
Artery: A vessel that carries blood away from the heart.
Artery - Of The Teeth: Refers to the arteries supplying blood to the teeth, primarily the maxillary artery.
Astragalus (of the foot): Also known as the talus bone, it forms part of the ankle joint.
Atlas (cervical vertebra): The first cervical vertebra of the spine, supporting the skull.
Atrium (left): The upper left chamber of the heart that receives oxygenated blood from the lungs.
Atrium (right): The upper right chamber of the heart that receives deoxygenated blood from the body.
Auricle (of the heart): A small muscular appendage of each atrium in the heart.
Back: The posterior part of the human body, running from the neck to the pelvis.
Backbone: The spine or vertebral column; the series of vertebrae extending from the skull to the lower back.
Backbone/Spine: Another term for the vertebral column or spine.
Beard: The hair growing on the chin and lower cheeks of a man's face.
Belly (stomach & bowel): Refers to the abdomen, particularly the front part where the stomach and intestines are located.
Belly Button (see navel): The small, round scar on the abdomen where the umbilical cord was attached.
Belly Button (protrude): Refers to a navel that sticks out.
Biceps: The large muscle at the front of the upper arm responsible for bending the arm.
Bicuspids: The two-cusped teeth located between the canines and molars, also known as premolars.
Big Toe: The largest toe on the foot.
Bile: A digestive fluid produced by the liver and stored in the gallbladder, essential for the digestion of fats.
Bile Duct: The duct that carries bile from the liver and gallbladder to the duodenum.
Bladder: The organ that stores urine before it is excreted from the body.
Blood: The red liquid that circulates in the arteries and veins, carrying oxygen and nutrients to the body and removing waste.
Blood Clot: A thickened mass in the blood formed by platelets to stop bleeding.
Blood Vessel: Any of the tubes through which blood circulates in the body, including arteries, veins, and capillaries.
Body: The physical structure of a person or an animal, including the bones, flesh, and organs.
Body (dead): Refers to a corpse or the remains of a dead person or animal.
Bone: The hard, rigid form of connective tissue constituting most of the skeleton.
Bone Marrow, Marrow: The soft, spongy tissue in the center of bones where blood cells are produced.
Bones: The rigid organs that constitute part of the vertebrate skeleton, supporting and protecting various parts of the body.
Bottom: The lower part of something; in anatomy, often refers to the buttocks.
Bottom, Backside: Another term for the buttocks or the rear part of the body.
Bowel: The intestine, especially the lower part of the digestive system, including the large intestine.
Brain: The organ in the skull that controls all bodily functions and mental processes.
Brainstem: The central trunk of the brain, continuing downward to form the spinal cord.
Breast: The front of the chest, especially the mammary glands in women.
Breast of a Woman: Refers specifically to the mammary glands in females.
Breastbone (sternum): The long flat bone in the center of the chest to which the ribs are attached.

terms.english: bronchi (larger air passages in the lungs
terms.en_def: Bronchi (larger air passages in the lungs): The major air passages of the lungs that branch off from the windpipe (trachea).

terms.english: bronchioles (smaller air passages in the lungs)
terms.en_def: Bronchioles (smaller air passages in the lungs): The tiny branches of air tubes within the lungs that connect to the alveoli.
Bronchus: One of the two main branches of the trachea that lead to the lungs.
Brow: The area of the face above the eyes, including the eyebrows.
Buccal Cavity (mouth cavity): The mouth, including the space between the teeth and the inner cheeks.
Buttocks: The fleshy part of the body at the back of the hips, often referred to as the rear or backside.
Caecum: A pouch connected to the junction of the small and large intestines.
Calcaneum (of the foot): The heel bone, also known as the calcaneus.
Calcaneus: The largest bone in the foot, forming the heel.
Calf: The back portion of the lower leg.
Calf (of the leg): The muscular back part of the lower leg, primarily made up of the gastrocnemius and soleus muscles.
Canine tooth: The pointed teeth located between the incisors and premolars, used for tearing food.
Capillary: The smallest blood vessels where oxygen and nutrients are exchanged with tissues.

terms.tongan: kālava 'o e kia´ mei he mafu´
terms.en_def: Carotic artery: A major artery in the neck that supplies blood to the brain, neck, and face.
Carpal: Refers to the bones of the wrist.
Cartilage: A flexible connective tissue found in joints, ear, nose, and other areas of the body.
Cartilage permanent: Cartilage that remains throughout life, such as the cartilage in the ear and nose.
Cartilage temporary: Cartilage that is eventually replaced by bone, such as during the development of long bones.
Cecum (beginning of large intestine): The first section of the large intestine, where the small intestine joins the large intestine.
Cell: The basic structural, functional, and biological unit of all living organisms.
Cement (of the teeth): A calcified substance covering the root of a tooth, helping to anchor it to the jawbone.
Cerebellum: A part of the brain responsible for coordinating voluntary movements and balance.
Cerebral hemisphere: One of the two halves of the brain that control different functions and processes.
Cerebrum: The largest part of the brain, responsible for cognitive functions such as thought, memory, and emotion.
Cervical Vertebrae: The seven vertebrae in the neck region of the spine.
Cervix: The lower part of the uterus that opens into the vagina.
Cheek: The soft area of the face below the eyes, above the jaw, and to the side of the nose and mouth.
Chest: The front part of the body between the neck and the abdomen, housing the heart and lungs.
Chin: The lower part of the face below the mouth, formed by the lower jawbone.

terms.english: chordae tendineae - tendinus cords or heart strings
terms.en_def: Chordae tendineae (tendinous cords or heart strings): Thin, strong cords that connect the heart valves to the heart muscles, preventing them from inverting.
Clavicle (collar bone): A long bone that serves as a strut between the shoulder blade and the sternum.
Clitoris: A small, sensitive, erectile part of the female genitalia.
Coccyx (tailbone): The small, triangular bone at the base of the spinal column, composed of fused vertebrae.
Colon: The longest part of the large intestine, involved in water absorption and formation of feces.
Cornea (of the eye): The transparent, dome-shaped surface that covers the front of the eye and helps focus light.
Coronary artery (left): The artery that supplies oxygen-rich blood to the left side of the heart muscle.
Coronary artery (right): The artery that supplies oxygen-rich blood to the right side of the heart muscle.

terms.english: corpus callosum (nerve fibres connecting brain hemispheres)
terms.en_def: Corpus callosum (nerve fibers connecting brain hemispheres): A thick band of nerve fibers that connects the left and right hemispheres of the brain, facilitating communication between them.
Corpuscles: Cells or cell-like structures, particularly red or white blood cells.
Cranial nerves: Twelve pairs of nerves that emerge directly from the brain and control functions such as smell, vision, and facial movements.
Cranium (skull): The bony structure that encloses and protects the brain.
Crown (of the teeth): The visible part of the tooth above the gum line.
Crutch: A support used by an individual to aid in walking, typically placed under the arms.
Cuboid (of the foot): One of the tarsal bones located on the outer side of the foot.
Cuneiform (of the hand): The wedge-shaped bones in the wrist (carpal bones) and foot (tarsal bones).
Cusps (of the teeth): The pointed or rounded projections on the chewing surface of the teeth.
Cuticle: The thin layer of skin at the base of the nails.
Deltoid (shoulder muscles): The large, triangular muscles covering the shoulder joint.
Dentin(e) (of the teeth): The hard tissue beneath the enamel and cementum of a tooth, making up the bulk of the tooth structure.
Dermis (layer of skin): The thick layer of living tissue below the epidermis, containing blood vessels, nerves, and glands.
Diaphragm: The dome-shaped muscle that separates the chest cavity from the abdominal cavity, playing a key role in breathing.

terms.tongan: uoua holisi vaha'a 'o e kete mo e fatafata´

terms.en_def: Digestive canal/system: The system of organs responsible for processing food, absorbing nutrients, and eliminating waste.
Dorsal Vertebrae: The vertebrae located in the upper and mid-back (thoracic vertebrae).
Duodenum: The first part of the small intestine, where the stomach empties its contents.
Ear: The organ responsible for hearing and balance, divided into outer, middle, and inner sections.
Ear inner: The part of the ear containing the cochlea and semicircular canals, involved in hearing and balance.
Ear middle: The air-filled space behind the eardrum that contains the ossicles, which transmit sound vibrations.
Ear outer: The external part of the ear, including the auricle (pinna) and ear canal.
Eardrum: A thin membrane that separates the outer ear from the middle ear and vibrates in response to sound.
Earlobe: The soft, fleshy lower part of the ear.
Eggs, Ova: The female reproductive cells produced in the ovaries.
Elbow: The joint connecting the upper arm to the forearm.
Elbow joint (inner side): The inner aspect of the elbow, where the forearm muscles attach to the upper arm.
Enamel (of the teeth): The hard, outer surface layer of a tooth that provides protection.
End of penis: The tip of the male genital organ.
Endocardium (inner lining of the heart): The thin layer of tissue lining the inside of the heart chambers.
Epidermis (outer layer of skin): The outermost layer of skin, providing a protective barrier.
Epiglottis (flap in the throat): A leaf-shaped flap of cartilage that covers the windpipe during swallowing to prevent food from entering the lungs.
Esophagus/Oesophagus: The muscular tube that carries food and liquids from the throat to the stomach.
Ethmoid (of the skull): A delicate bone located at the roof of the nose, separating the nasal cavity from the brain.
External cuneiform (of the foot): One of the three cuneiform bones in the foot, located on the lateral side.
Eye: The organ of sight.
Eye pupil: The black circular opening in the center of the iris, controlling the amount of light entering the eye.
Eyeball: The spherical structure of the eye, containing the lens, retina, and other components necessary for vision.
Eyebrow: The strip of hair growing on the ridge above the eye socket.
Eyelash: The short hairs growing on the edge of the eyelids, protecting the eyes from dust and debris.
Eyelid: The movable fold of skin that covers and protects the eye.
Face: The front part of the head, including the eyes, nose, mouth, and forehead.
Faeces: Solid waste material expelled from the digestive tract through the anus.
Fallopian Tubes: The pair of tubes that carry eggs from the ovaries to the uterus.
Fat: A type of tissue that stores energy and insulates the body.
Fatty tissue: A type of body tissue that stores fat, providing energy and insulation for the body.
Feet, Foot: The lower extremities used for standing, walking, and running.
Femur (thigh bone): The longest and strongest bone in the body, extending from the hip to the knee.
A developing baby inside the womb from about eight weeks after conception until birth.

terms.english: fibrin - fatu vave ai e toto
terms.en_def: Fibrin: A protein involved in blood clotting.
Fibro cartilage: A type of cartilage that is tough and flexible, found in areas like the intervertebral discs.

terms.tongan: hui 'alu mei he mu'a tui ki he va'e
terms.en_def: Fibula (calf bone): The smaller of the two bones in the lower leg, located on the lateral side.
Finger: One of the five digits on the hand.
Little finger: The smallest finger, located on the outermost side of the hand.
Short finger (cut): A finger that has been partially amputated, resulting in a shorter length.
Thumb: The short, thick first digit of the hand, opposable to the other fingers, allowing for gripping and handling objects.
Finger bones: The phalanges, the bones of the fingers.
Finger index: The second finger, located next to the thumb.
Finger middle: The third finger, located between the index and ring fingers.
Finger pinky: The smallest finger, located on the outermost side of the hand.
Finger ring: The fourth finger, located between the middle and pinky fingers.
Fingernail: The hard, protective covering at the tip of each finger.
Fingertips: The sensitive pads at the tips of the fingers.
Fist: The hand closed tightly with the fingers curled inward.
Flesh: The soft tissue of the body, consisting of muscle and fat.
Follicles (hair roots): The small cavities in the skin where hair grows.
Foot: The lower extremity below the ankle, used for standing, walking, and running.
Foot (sole of): The bottom part of the foot.
Forearm: The part of the arm between the elbow and the wrist.
Forefinger: Another term for the index finger.
Forehead: The part of the face above the eyebrows and below the hairline.
Frontal (of the skull): The bone forming the front part of the skull and the upper part of the eye sockets.
Gall bladder: A small organ that stores bile produced by the liver.
Gastrocnemius (calf muscle): The large muscle at the back of the lower leg that forms part of the calf.
Genitals: The external organs of the reproductive system.
Gingival sulcus (of the teeth): The small gap between the teeth and gums.
Gland: An organ that produces and releases substances, such as hormones or enzymes.
Glands: Organs that secrete hormones, enzymes, or other substances.
Glottis (part of the larynx): The part of the larynx containing the vocal cords, responsible for sound production.
Groin: The area of the body where the thigh meets the abdomen.
Gum: The soft tissue that surrounds and supports the teeth.
Hair: The thread-like strands growing from the skin, particularly on the head.
Hair of the head: The hair that grows on the scalp.
Hamstring: The muscles at the back of the thigh that bend the knee and extend the hip.
Hand: The part of the body at the end of the arm, used for grasping and manipulating objects.
Hand - back of the: The dorsal side of the hand, opposite the palm.
Hand - front of the hand: The palmar side of the hand, where the palm is located.
Hand bones (see metacarpal): The bones that make up the hand, including the metacarpals.
Head: The uppermost part of the body, containing the brain, eyes, ears, nose, and mouth.

terms.tongan: ongo'i, telinga tu'a, telinga veiveiua, telinga loto
terms.en_def: Hearing: The sense that detects sound.
Heart: The muscular organ that pumps blood throughout the body.
Heel: The back part of the foot, below the ankle.
Hip: The area on either side of the pelvis, where the thigh bone meets the pelvis.
Hip bone: The large, flat bone forming the sides of the pelvis.
Hormone: A chemical messenger produced by glands that regulates various functions in the body.
Humerus (upper arm bone): The bone in the upper arm, extending from the shoulder to the elbow.
Ilium (part of the pelvis): The large, broad bone forming the upper part of the pelvis.
Incisor: A type of tooth located at the front of the mouth, used for cutting food.
Index finger: The second finger, located next to the thumb.
Inferior vena cava: The large vein that carries deoxygenated blood from the lower body to the heart.
Intestine - large: The part of the digestive system that absorbs water and forms feces.
Intestine: The digestive tube that extends from the stomach to the anus, including both the small and large intestines.
Intestine - small: The part of the digestive system where most digestion and absorption of nutrients occurs.
Internal Organs: Vital body parts located inside the body, such as the heart, lungs, liver, kidneys, and intestines, that perform essential functions for survival.
Iris: The colored part of the eye that controls the size of the pupil.
Ischium: The lower, curved part of the pelvis, on which the body sits.
Jaw: The bones forming the framework of the mouth, including the upper jaw (maxilla) and lower jaw (mandible).
Jawbone: Another term for the mandible, the lower jawbone.
Jejunum: The middle section of the small intestine.
Joints: The points where two or more bones meet, allowing for movement.

terms.tongan: kālava 'o e kia ki he mafu´
terms.en_def: Jugular vein: The large vein in the neck that carries blood from the head to the heart.
Kidney: The organ that filters waste from the blood and produces urine.
Knee: The joint connecting the thigh to the lower leg.
Knee cap: The patella, the small bone that covers the knee joint.
Knuckle: The joint of a finger, especially where the finger bends.
Lachrymal (of the face): Relating to the glands that produce tears.
Large Instestine: The part of the digestive system that absorbs water and forms feces.
Larynx: The voice box, located in the throat, containing the vocal cords.
Left auricle: The left upper chamber of the heart that receives oxygenated blood from the lungs.
Left ventricle: The left lower chamber of the heart that pumps oxygenated blood to the body.
Leg: The lower limb of the body, from the hip to the foot.
Ligament: A band of tough, fibrous tissue that connects bones or supports organs.
Lips: The fleshy, movable parts of the mouth that form the opening.
Liver: A large organ that processes nutrients, detoxifies the blood, and produces bile.
Loins: The lower part of the back and the sides of the body between the ribs and pelvis.
Lower jaw: The mandible, the bone forming the lower part of the skull.
Lower maxillary (of the face): The lower jawbone or mandible.
Lumbar Vertebrae: The five vertebrae in the lower back.
Lungs: The pair of organs responsible for gas exchange, taking in oxygen and expelling carbon dioxide.
Lymph glands: Small glands that are part of the immune system, filtering lymph fluid and housing immune cells.
Malar (of the face): Relating to the cheekbone.
Marrow, Bone Marrow: The soft, spongy tissue inside bones where blood cells are produced.
Medulla oblongata: The lower part of the brainstem that controls vital functions like breathing and heart rate.
Membrane: A thin layer of tissue that covers a surface or lines a cavity or organ.
Metacarpal (hand bones): The five long bones in the hand that connect the wrist to the fingers.
Metatarsal (foot bones): The five long bones in the foot that connect the ankle to the toes.
Middle Cuneiform (of the foot): The middle of the three cuneiform bones in the foot.
Mind: The set of cognitive faculties that enables consciousness, perception, thinking, and memory.
Molars: The large, flat teeth at the back of the mouth used for grinding food.
Mouth: The opening in the face through which food is taken in and vocal sounds are emitted.
Mucous membrane: The lining of various body passages that produce mucus to protect and lubricate.
Muscle: A tissue composed of fibers that contract to produce movement in the body.
Muscles - extensor: Muscles that extend or straighten a limb or body part.
Muscles - involuntary: Muscles that contract without conscious control, such as those in the heart and digestive system.
Muscles - voluntary: Muscles that are under conscious control, such as those used for movement.
Nail: The hard, keratinous covering on the tips of fingers and toes.
Nape (back of the neck): The back of the neck, just below the hairline.
Nasal (of the face): Relating to the nose.
Nasal cavity: The hollow space behind the nose that filters, warms, and moistens inhaled air.
Navel: The belly button, the scar on the abdomen where the umbilical cord was attached.
Neck: The part of the body connecting the head to the torso.
Nerve: Bundles of fibers that transmit electrical signals between the brain and the rest of the body.
Nipple: The small projection in the center of the breast, through which milk can be secreted.
Nodes (lymph nodes): Small, bean-shaped glands that filter lymph fluid and house white blood cells.
Nose: The organ on the face that detects smell and allows for breathing.
Nostrils: The two openings of the nose through which air enters and exits.
Occipital (of the skull): The bone at the back and base of the skull.
Occiput (back of the head): The posterior part of the skull.
Occlusal (biting) surface (of the teeth): The surface of a tooth that comes into contact with the teeth of the opposite jaw during biting or chewing.
Oesophagus: The tube that carries food and liquids from the throat to the stomach.
Olecranon (elbow bone): The bony prominence of the elbow, where the humerus and ulna meet.
Optic nerve: The nerve that transmits visual information from the retina to the brain.
Organ: A part of the body that performs a specific function, such as the heart or liver.
Os Coccygis (tailbone): The small, triangular bone at the base of the spine, also known as the coccyx.
Os Hyoides: The hyoid bone, a U-shaped bone in the neck that supports the tongue.
Os Magnum (of the hand): Another term for the capitate bone, the largest of the carpal bones in the hand.
Os Sacrum: The large, triangular bone at the base of the spine, above the coccyx.
Ossa Innominata: The two large bones that make up the sides of your pelvis. They are also called hip bones
Ovary: The female reproductive organ that produces eggs and hormones.
Ovum (plural: ova): The female reproductive cell, also known as an egg.
Palate: The roof of the mouth, separating the oral and nasal cavities, and involved in taste perception.
Palate (of the face): The roof of the mouth, separating the oral and nasal cavities.
Palm: The inner surface of the hand between the fingers and the wrist.
Palm bones: The five metacarpal bones in the hand that connect the wrist to the fingers, providing structure and support to the palm.
Pancreas: The gland behind the stomach that produces digestive enzymes and insulin.
Parietal (of the skull): The two bones that form the sides and top of the skull.
Parotid: The largest of the salivary glands, located near the ear.
Patella (kneecap): The small, flat bone that covers and protects the knee joint.
Pelvis: The lower part of the torso, consisting of the hip bones, sacrum, and coccyx.
Penis: The male external reproductive organ.
Pericardium: The double-walled sac that encloses the heart.
Periodontal membrane (of the teeth): The connective tissue that surrounds the roots of the teeth and attaches them to the jawbone.
Periosteum (bony tissue) (of the teeth): The dense layer of connective tissue covering the surface of a bone.
Peritoneum (lining of the abdominal cavity): The membrane that lines the abdominal cavity and covers the abdominal organs.
Permanent cartilage: Cartilage that remains throughout life, as opposed to temporary cartilage, which is eventually replaced by bone.
Phalanges (finger bones): The bones that make up the fingers.
Phalanges (toe bones): The bones that make up the toes.
Pharynx (throat): The muscular tube that connects the mouth and nasal passages to the esophagus and larynx.

Involuntary urination during sleep in children, typically after the age at which they are expected to remain dry overnight.
A sudden weakness or paralysis of the muscles on one side of the face, usually temporary and linked to nerve damage.
A condition causing brief episodes of dizziness or vertigo due to changes in head position, caused by inner ear issues.
A mental health condition marked by extreme mood swings, including emotional highs (mania) and lows (depression).
Abnormalities in physical or mental development present at birth, caused by genetic or environmental factors.
A temporary loss of consciousness or memory, often due to fainting, low blood sugar, or alcohol/drug use.
The loss of blood from the circulatory system, which can be internal or external.
Postcoital bleeding, which can be caused by various conditions, including infections, injury, or cervical issues.
Inflammation of the eyelids, often causing redness, swelling, itching, and flaky skin around the eyes.
A condition of significant vision impairment that cannot be corrected fully with glasses or contact lenses.
Small fluid-filled sacs on the skin caused by friction, burns, or infections.
A feeling of fullness or blockage in the ear, often caused by earwax buildup, infections, or pressure changes.
Nasal congestion or a feeling of blockage in the nose due to colds, allergies, or sinus infections.
A medical procedure where diseased or damaged bone marrow is replaced with healthy blood-forming cells.
Clumps of blood that have changed from liquid to gel-like, which can form in veins or arteries and block blood flow.
The presence of blood in the urine, which may indicate a urinary tract infection, kidney stones, or other underlying conditions.
A severe and life-threatening condition also known as sepsis, caused by bacteria or toxins entering the bloodstream.
The force exerted by circulating blood on the walls of blood vessels, measured in millimeters of mercury (mmHg).
Also known as hypertension, it refers to elevated pressure in the arteries, which can lead to heart disease or stroke.
Also known as hypotension, it refers to lower-than-normal pressure in the arteries, which may cause dizziness or fainting.
A medical procedure where donated blood is given to a person who needs it, typically due to severe blood loss or illness.
A measure of body fat based on height and weight, used to assess whether a person is underweight, normal weight, overweight, or obese.
An unpleasant smell emanating from the body, often caused by the breakdown of sweat by bacteria on the skin.
Painful, pus-filled bumps under the skin caused by bacterial infections in hair follicles or oil glands.
A mental health disorder characterized by unstable moods, behavior, and relationships, along with difficulties in regulating emotions.
Cancer that begins in the large intestine (colon) or rectum, often detected by changes in bowel habits or bleeding.
A medical process used to detect early signs of bowel cancer, typically through stool tests or colonoscopy.
Small clumps of cells that form on the lining of the colon or rectum, some of which can become cancerous over time.
Damage to the brain caused by trauma, illness, or lack of oxygen, which can lead to physical, cognitive, or emotional impairments.
A painful, pus-filled infection in the breast tissue, often linked to breastfeeding or mastitis.
A type of cancer that forms in the cells of the breasts, commonly presenting as a lump or abnormal mammogram.
Medical interventions used to treat breast cancer, including surgery, chemotherapy, radiation, and hormone therapy.
An infection in the breast tissue, often occurring in breastfeeding women, leading to pain, swelling, and redness.
Abnormalities in breast tissue, which may include benign cysts or cancerous growths.
Discomfort or pain in one or both breasts, which can be caused by hormonal changes, injury, or underlying conditions.
The number of breaths taken per minute, used to assess respiratory function in medical settings.
A sensation of shortness of breath or difficulty breathing, which can be caused by respiratory, heart, or other conditions.
A fracture in the upper part of the thigh bone (femur) near the hip joint, commonly occurring in older adults due to falls.
A fracture or break in the bones of the nose, often resulting from trauma or injury.
A fracture in one or more of the bones in the wrist, typically caused by falls or accidents.
A chronic condition where the bronchial tubes of the lungs become damaged and widened, leading to persistent cough and mucus production.
The same condition as bronchiectasis but occurring in children, often due to genetic or early lung infections.
A viral infection that causes inflammation of the small airways in the lungs, common in infants and young children.
Inflammation of the bronchial tubes, typically caused by infection, leading to cough and mucus production.
An eating disorder characterized by binge eating followed by purging through vomiting, excessive exercise, or laxative use.
A bony bump that forms at the base of the big toe, often caused by wearing tight shoes or due to genetic factors.
Immediate care for burns, typically involving cooling the area, covering it, and seeking medical help if necessary.
Inflammation of the bursa, a small fluid-filled sac that cushions bones and tendons near joints, often caused by overuse or injury.
Thickened areas of skin that form due to repeated pressure or friction, commonly on the feet or hands.
A type of bacteria that causes gastrointestinal infections, often from contaminated food or water.
A disease in which abnormal cells grow uncontrollably and can invade or spread to other parts of the body.
A cluster of boils (pus-filled bumps) connected under the skin, caused by bacterial infection.
A sudden stop in heart function, leading to loss of consciousness and lack of pulse, often requiring immediate medical intervention.
A distinction between a heart attack (myocardial infarction), where blood flow is restricted, and cardiac arrest, where the heart suddenly stops beating, requiring immediate resuscitation.
A medical evaluation to estimate a person’s risk of developing heart disease based on factors like cholesterol levels, blood pressure, and lifestyle.
A condition caused by pressure on the median nerve in the wrist, leading to pain, numbness, and weakness in the hand.
A clouding of the lens in the eye that leads to a decrease in vision, often associated with aging.
A bacterial skin infection that causes redness, swelling, and pain, commonly affecting the legs.
A group of disorders that affect movement, muscle tone, and posture, caused by damage to the developing brain.
Cancer that develops in the cervix, often linked to human papillomavirus (HPV) infection.
A condition where cells from the inside of the cervix spread to the outside, causing discharge or bleeding.
Small, benign growths on the cervix, often causing no symptoms but sometimes leading to abnormal bleeding.
A genetic disorder that causes damage to the peripheral nerves, leading to muscle weakness and loss of sensation in the limbs.
Infections that affect the lungs or airways, such as bronchitis or pneumonia, causing cough, mucus, and breathing difficulties.
Discomfort or pain felt in the chest, which can be caused by heart, lung, muscle, or digestive issues.
A highly contagious viral infection that causes an itchy rash and flu-like symptoms, most common in children.
Small, itchy, and painful red or purple bumps on the skin caused by exposure to cold and damp conditions.
Physical, emotional, or sexual harm inflicted on a child by an adult or caregiver.
Cancers that occur in children, which differ in type and treatment from adult cancers.
Vaccinations given to children to protect against infectious diseases like measles, mumps, and polio.
Various skin conditions in children that cause red, itchy, or raised patches, often due to infections, allergies, or irritants.
A sexually transmitted bacterial infection that can cause genital pain and discharge, often asymptomatic.
A waxy, fat-like substance found in cells, necessary for building cells but harmful in excess.
A long-term inflammation of the bronchial tubes, causing cough and mucus production, often linked to smoking.

terms.tongan: Mahakitauhi Sinitolome Hakinekina/ Mahaki Lolomai by Mapa
terms.en_def: A complex disorder characterized by extreme fatigue that doesn’t improve with rest and may worsen with physical or mental activity.
A long-term condition in which the kidneys do not work as well as they should to filter waste from the blood.
A group of lung diseases, including emphysema and chronic bronchitis, that cause breathing difficulties.
A late stage of liver scarring (fibrosis) caused by many forms of liver diseases and conditions, such as hepatitis or chronic alcoholism.
A bacterial infection that causes severe diarrhea and inflammation of the colon, often after antibiotic use.
A severe, recurring headache that occurs in clusters, often around one eye, typically lasting for weeks or months.
A medical device surgically implanted to help individuals with severe hearing loss by directly stimulating the auditory nerve.
A general description of coeliac disease, a condition where gluten intake damages the small intestine.
A form of psychotherapy that helps individuals identify and change negative thought patterns to improve mental health.
Painful blisters on or around the lips, caused by the herpes simplex virus (HSV).
A common viral infection affecting the nose and throat, causing symptoms like a runny nose, sneezing, and coughing.
Severe, often fluctuating pain in the abdomen caused by the intestines, common in infants.
A chronic pain condition affecting a limb, often after injury or surgery, with symptoms like swelling and changes in skin color.
Specially designed stockings that help improve blood flow and reduce swelling in the legs, often used for varicose veins or after surgery.
A mild traumatic brain injury caused by a blow or jolt to the head, leading to temporary loss of normal brain function.
A barrier method of contraception that prevents sperm from entering the vagina, also reducing the risk of sexually transmitted infections (STIs).
A group of abnormalities in the heart's structure present at birth, affecting how blood flows through the heart.
Inflammation or infection of the conjunctiva (the white part of the eye), causing redness, swelling, and discharge; also known as "pink eye."
The voluntary agreement to a medical procedure or treatment after being fully informed of the risks and benefits.
Difficulty in passing stools or infrequent bowel movements, commonly caused by lack of fiber, dehydration, or certain medications.
Thin, curved lenses worn directly on the eyes to correct vision problems such as nearsightedness, farsightedness, or astigmatism.
A method of tracking blood glucose levels in real time using a sensor placed under the skin, commonly used in diabetes management.
A treatment for sleep apnea that uses mild air pressure to keep the airways open during sleep.
Methods or devices used to prevent pregnancy, including pills, condoms, IUDs, and implants.
Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, a progressive lung disease that causes breathing difficulties, commonly associated with smoking.
A condition where the heart's arteries become narrowed or blocked, reducing blood flow to the heart muscle and leading to chest pain or heart attack.
COVID-19 is the disease caused by the SARS-CoV-2 coronavirus. It usually spreads between people in close contact.
A condition where individuals continue to experience symptoms of COVID-19 long after the initial infection has cleared.
An immune response to proteins found in cow's milk, causing symptoms such as rash, vomiting, and breathing difficulties.
A condition where the skin on the heel becomes dry and cracked, sometimes leading to pain or infection.
A type of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) that causes chronic inflammation of the gastrointestinal tract, leading to symptoms like abdominal pain and diarrhea.
A viral infection in children causing a distinctive barking cough and difficulty breathing, often worse at night.
A parasitic infection causing diarrhea, often spread through contaminated water or food.
A heart scan that measures the amount of calcium in the coronary arteries, used to assess the risk of coronary artery disease.
A condition caused by prolonged exposure to high levels of cortisol, leading to symptoms like weight gain, high blood pressure, and fragile skin.
Minor injuries to the skin caused by sharp objects or friction, often easily treated at home with cleaning and bandaging.
A genetic disorder that affects the lungs and digestive system, causing thick, sticky mucus buildup, leading to respiratory and digestive problems.
Inflammation of the bladder, usually caused by a bacterial infection, leading to painful urination and frequent urge to urinate.
A common virus that usually causes mild or no symptoms but can be serious in newborns or individuals with weakened immune systems.
A common scalp condition where small pieces of dry skin flake off, often causing itching.
A painful condition affecting the tendons on the thumb side of the wrist, causing swelling and difficulty moving the thumb.
Partial or total inability to hear, ranging from mild hearing loss to complete hearing impairment.
A blood clot that forms in a deep vein, usually in the legs, which can cause pain and swelling, and may lead to serious complications if the clot travels to the lungs.
A condition that occurs when the body loses more fluids than it takes in, causing symptoms such as dry mouth, fatigue, and dizziness.
A sudden, severe confusion and rapid changes in brain function, often caused by illness, infection, or medication, particularly in elderly individuals.
A psychotic disorder where individuals can’t tell what’s real from what is imagined.
A general description of dementia, a decline in cognitive function severe enough to interfere with daily life, caused by various diseases affecting the brain.
A mosquito-borne viral infection causing symptoms like high fever, severe headache, pain behind the eyes, joint and muscle pain, and rash.
A general description of depression, a common mental health disorder characterized by persistent sadness, loss of interest, and changes in sleep, appetite, or energy levels.
Depression that affects young people, often presenting with irritability, withdrawal from social activities, and changes in academic performance.
Resources and support for young individuals experiencing depression, offering guidance on how to cope, seek help, and improve mental well-being.
Depression occurring in older adults, which can be influenced by factors such as isolation, chronic illness, and life changes.
Depression that occurs during pregnancy or after childbirth (postpartum), affecting a person's mood and ability to care for themselves and their baby.
Inflammation of the skin, causing redness, itching, and sometimes blistering or peeling, often triggered by allergies, irritants, or underlying conditions like eczema.
Complications of diabetes that can affect the eyes, including retinopathy, cataracts, and glaucoma.
An open sore on the foot that occurs due to diabetes-related nerve damage or poor circulation, often difficult to heal.
A type of diabetes that develops during pregnancy, potentially leading to complications if not managed properly.
Nerve damage (neuropathy) caused by prolonged high blood sugar, leading to symptoms like numbness, tingling, or pain, especially in the feet and hands.
A condition where blood sugar levels are higher than normal but not high enough to be classified as diabetes, often a warning sign for future diabetes.
A general explanation of type 1 diabetes, an autoimmune condition where the body attacks insulin-producing cells in the pancreas and insulin is not produced.
A general description of type 2 diabetes, where the body becomes resistant to insulin or doesn't produce enough insulin.
A condition where high blood sugar levels develop during pregnancy (gestational diabetes) or pre-existing diabetes needs special management.
Techniques and habits for individuals to manage their diabetes, including monitoring blood glucose, taking medication, and maintaining a healthy lifestyle.
A dangerous condition where the body produces high levels of blood acids (ketones), often occurring when diabetes is not managed properly.
Kidney damage caused by diabetes, which can lead to kidney failure if not treated.
A diabetes complication that affects the eyes, caused by damage to the blood vessels in the retina, which can lead to blindness if untreated.
A treatment that performs the function of the kidneys when they fail, filtering waste and excess fluids from the blood.
Frequent, loose, or watery bowel movements, often caused by infection, diet, or certain medical conditions.
A serious bacterial infection that affects the mucous membranes of the throat and nose, leading to difficulty breathing, heart failure, and paralysis.
An injury where a joint is forced out of normal position. Prompt medical attention is required to put the joint back in place.
A condition where small pouches (diverticula) form in the walls of the colon, sometimes becoming inflamed or infected (diverticulitis).
A genetic disorder caused by the presence of an extra copy of chromosome 21, leading to developmental delays and physical features characteristic of the condition.
A condition where the eyes don't produce enough tears or the tears evaporate too quickly, leading to irritation, redness, and discomfort.
A condition where the mouth doesn't produce enough saliva, leading to difficulty swallowing, speaking, and an increased risk of dental problems.
A condition where the fingers become permanently bent due to thickening of the connective tissue in the palm, limiting hand movement.
Deep vein thrombosis, a blood clot that forms in a deep vein, typically in the legs during or after a hospital stay or long flights/trips.

A learning disorder characterised by difficulty reading and writing. Dyslexia occurs in children with normal vision and intelligence.
